info.title: TCP Port Scanner
info.description: Give this API a hostname or IP address and it will try connecting to each port in your requested range. For every port that answers, it tells you whether it is open or blocked, which service is likely running there (like a web server or SSH), and what software version was detected. This saves you from installing network tools, parsing messy command-line output, or writing socket loops yourself. Only scan hosts you own or have permission to scan — this tool does not check that for you.
info.x-guidance: POST a JSON body with 'target' (hostname or IP as a string) and optionally 'ports' (a range like '1-1000' or a comma-separated list like '22,80,443'), 'scan_type' (only 'tcp_connect' is supported), and 'timeout' (whole number of seconds, 5 to 60). The response includes an 'open_ports' array — each item has 'port', 'protocol', 'state', 'service', and 'version'. Use 'ports_scanned' and 'closed_or_filtered_count' for summary stats. If the target cannot be reached or resolved, you will receive a 400 error with a plain-English 'error' field. Never use this on hosts you do not own or have explicit permission to scan.

port.title: Port
port.description: The port number that is open.

protocol.title: Protocol
protocol.description: The network protocol used (always 'tcp' for this scan type).

service.title: Service
service.description: The name of the service most likely running on this port, like 'ssh' or 'http'.

version.title: Version
version.description: The software version detected on this port, if any. May be empty if not detectable.

target.title: Target
target.description: The hostname (like 'example.com') or numeric IP address (like '93.184.216.34') you want to scan. Must be a real, reachable address.

ports.title: Ports
ports.description: Which ports to check. Use a range like '1-1000', a comma-separated list like '22,80,443', or leave this out to automatically check the 1000 most commonly used ports.

scan_type.title: Scan Type
scan_type.description: How to probe each port. The only supported value right now is 'tcp_connect'. Defaults to 'tcp_connect' if left out.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: How many seconds the scan is allowed to run before giving up. Must be between 5 and 60. Defaults to 30 if left out.

target.title: Target
target.description: The hostname or IP address that was scanned, echoed back from your request.

resolved_ip.title: Resolved Ip
resolved_ip.description: The numeric IP address the hostname was resolved to before scanning.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: How long the scan took in milliseconds.

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: True if every requested port was scanned. False if the time budget ran out and only part of the range was probed — in that case the open_ports listed are still accurate, but ports NOT listed may be unscanned rather than closed.

ports_requested.title: Ports Requested
ports_requested.description: How many ports you asked to scan.

ports_scanned.title: Ports Scanned
ports_scanned.description: How many ports were actually checked. Equals ports_requested on a complete scan; lower when the scan was cut short by the time budget.

open_ports.title: Open Ports
open_ports.description: Ports that responded as open, sorted from lowest to highest port number. Always trustworthy, even on an incomplete scan.

closed_or_filtered_count.title: Closed Or Filtered Count
closed_or_filtered_count.description: How many scanned ports were closed or blocked. On an incomplete scan this covers only the ports actually probed.

warning.title: Warning
warning.description: Present only when the scan did not fully complete. Explains what to do for full coverage.
